easy.def: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
examples: A lion is a predator.
A shark is a predator.
The mouse hid from the predator.

more.def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
examples: Owls are predators that hunt mice at night.
Wolves are predators that hunt in packs.
Without predators, there would be too many deer.

easy.def: To say what you think will happen.
examples: I predict it will rain today.
Can you predict the end of the story?
I predict we will win.

more.def: To say what you think will happen in the future, using what you already know.
examples: Scientists use clouds and wind to predict the weather.
No one can predict exactly when an earthquake will happen.
The teacher asked us to predict what would float.
We prepare for bed by brushing our teeth.
Dad prepares lunch.
We prepare for the trip.

more.def: To get ready for something, or to make something ready.
examples: The class prepared for the play by practicing every day.
The chef prepared a special meal.
The town prepared for the storm by stacking sandbags.
I got a present.
She wrapped the present.
The present was a book.

more.def: Something you give to someone to show love or thanks, usually on a special day.
examples: I wrapped a present for my sister's birthday.
He opened the present and found a toy train.
The best present was a visit from Grandma.
Everyone is present.
Is Sam present today?
All the kids were present.

more.def: Being in a place at a certain time.
examples: Every student was present on the day of the field trip.
Are all of the players present?
The teacher marked who was present.
For the present, we will stay inside.
Do not worry about tomorrow; think about the present.
The present is the time we live in.

more.def: The time that is happening now.
examples: At present, the museum is closed for repairs.
He lives in the present and does not worry about tomorrow.
Past, present and future are the three parts of time.
She will present the prize.
I present my report.
The class presents a play.

more.def: To give or show something to a group of people.
examples: The mayor will present the award to the winner.
Our class will present a play for the school.
She presented her science project to the judges.
The president gave a speech.
We pick a new president.
She wants to be president.

more.def: The elected leader of a country that has no king or queen.
examples: The president gave a speech to the whole nation.
Every four years, voters choose a new president.
The president met leaders from other countries.

easy.def: The person in charge of a club.
examples: Our class picked a president.
The president ran the meeting.
He is president of the chess club.

more.def: The person in charge of a club, a business or a school group.
examples: The president of the science club planned the field trip.
She was chosen president of the student council.
The president of the bank greeted the customers.
The flower is pretty.
She has a pretty dress.
What a pretty song!

more.def: Pleasing to look at or listen to, in a gentle way.
examples: The garden was pretty, with pink and yellow flowers.
She drew a pretty picture of the sunset.
The bird sang a pretty tune from the branch.

easy.def: A bit, but not a lot.
examples: It is pretty cold.
I am pretty tired.
The test was pretty easy.

more.def: To a fairly large degree, but not completely.
examples: The pond is pretty deep, so we stayed near the edge.
I was pretty sure that I had locked the door.
It is a pretty long walk to the library.

easy.def: Something hard that you must fix.
examples: We have a problem.
The problem is the door.
She fixed the problem.

more.def: Something that is hard to deal with and needs to be solved.
examples: The flat tire was a problem, so we called for help.
Our team worked together to solve the problem.
Litter on the beach is a problem for sea animals.

easy.def: A question to work out in math.
examples: I did the math problem.
This problem is hard.
Solve the problem.

more.def: A question or puzzle that you work out, especially in math.
examples: The teacher wrote a math problem on the board.
I solved the problem by drawing a picture.
Try the next problem on the page.

easy.def: To say you will really do something.
examples: I promise to feed the fish.
Promise you will come back.
She promised to share.

more.def: To tell someone that you will certainly do something.
examples: He promised to return the book by Friday.
The mayor promised to fix the roads.
I promise I will not tell anyone your secret.
A helmet protects your head.
Sunscreen protects your skin.
The dog protects the house.

more.def: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
examples: The mother bird protected her eggs from the cold.
Laws protect rare animals from hunters.
A shell protects the turtle's soft body.

easy.def: Feeling good about something you did.
examples: I am proud of my painting.
Dad is proud of me.
She was proud of her tall tower.

more.def: Feeling pleased about something you or someone else has done.
examples: Her parents were proud when she finished the race.
He is proud to be on the team.
The town is proud of its long history.
